question: What is the main job of peristalsis in the oesophagus?

options.A: Secreting digestive enzymes for protein breakdown
options.B: Propelling food downward into the stomach
options.C: Preventing air entry during the respiratory cycle
options.D: Absorbing water from swallowed liquid boluses

explanation: Peristalsis is made up of wave-like muscle contractions that push food along the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h1)

question: What usually happens when the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to stay closed?

options.B: Inability to swallow solid food particles
options.C: Rapid absorption of ingested oral medications
options.D: Obstruction of the upper respiratory airway

explanation: The lower oesophageal sphincter normally stops stomach contents from flowing backward, so when it relaxes, acid moves up and irritates the lining. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which test requires a patient to swallow a contrast liquid so X-rays can show narrow spots in the food pipe?
explanation: A barium swallow uses a special contrast liquid that shows up clearly on X-rays to highlight the shape and structure of the oesophagus. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why do doctors order an oesophageal manometry test?

options.B: Total daily exposure time to gastric acid
options.C: Presence of bleeding varices in the submucosa
options.D: Cellular dysplasia within mucosal tissue biopsies

explanation: Manometry measures how well the muscles in the oesophagus squeeze and coordinate during swallowing. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the medical name for the burning feeling in the chest known as heartburn?
explanation: Pyrosis is the clinical term for the burning discomfort behind the chest bone caused by stomach acid. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h3)

question: How does a hiatus hernia cause acid reflux?

options.A: By causing permanent paralysis of upper pharyngeal muscles
options.B: By disrupting the barrier function of the lower sphincter
options.C: By blocking the normal production of protective mucus
options.D: By increasing the total daily production of hydrochloric acid

explanation: When part of the stomach slides up through the diaphragm, the lower sphincter cannot close properly, allowing acid to leak upward. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the medical term for pain when swallowing food caused by an ulcer?
explanation: Odynophagia means painful swallowing due to inflammation or sores in the lining of the throat or food pipe. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why are proton pump inhibitors given to patients with oesophageal ulcers?

options.A: To reduce gastric acid secretion and allow mucosal healing
options.B: To stimulate rhythmic peristaltic contractions in smooth muscle
options.C: To physically coat the lower sphincter and prevent sliding
options.D: To directly kill fungal organisms causing local infection

explanation: Lowering the amount of acid in the stomach stops further irritation and gives the sore lining time to repair itself. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the main problem in achalasia during swallowing?

options.A: Failure of the lower sphincter to relax
options.B: Rapid perforation of the muscular wall
options.D: Excessive production of acidic gastric juice

explanation: In achalasia, the valve at the bottom of the food pipe does not open properly, trapping food inside. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h5)

question: Chest pain from severe oesophageal spasms must be carefully separated from which serious emergency?
explanation: Oesophageal spasms can cause chest discomfort that feels very similar to a heart attack, so careful checks are needed. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the main cause of oesophageal varices?

options.A: Chronic exposure to refluxed stomach acid
options.D: Bacterial infection of the mucosal lining

explanation: Liver problems increase pressure in the main blood vessels, forcing blood into smaller, fragile vessels in the lower oesophagus. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h6)

question: A patient is bleeding from oesophageal varices and showing low blood pressure. What is the immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Position the patient flat on their back without monitoring
options.B: Prepare the patient for routine barium swallow imaging
options.C: Encourage immediate oral fluid intake to replace blood loss
options.D: Maintain airway patency and support circulation with fluids

explanation: Severe bleeding puts breathing and blood flow at risk, making airway care and IV fluids the top emergency steps. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the usual first sign of oesophageal cancer?
explanation: As a growth makes the food pipe narrower, swallowing solid foods and later liquids slowly becomes harder. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which type of oesophageal cancer is most tied to long-term acid reflux and Barrett's oesophagus?
explanation: Adenocarcinoma typically develops in the lower part of the food pipe where constant acid exposure changes the normal cell lining. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's swallowing before letting them eat with an oesophageal condition?

options.A: To determine the exact pH level of gastric secretions
options.B: To measure the physical length of the oesophageal tube
options.C: To prevent the development of portal hypertension
options.D: To prevent aspiration of food into the respiratory tract

explanation: Poor swallowing ability means food can easily slip into the windpipe and cause a lung infection. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h8)

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient with mild acid reflux?

options.A: Wear tight abdominal binders to keep the stomach stable
options.B: Avoid lying down immediately after eating meals
options.C: Consume large, high-fat meals right before bedtime
options.D: Eliminate all physical exercise from daily routines

explanation: Staying upright after eating uses gravity to keep stomach acid down where it belongs. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h8)
